subject: Acme: promptset regression — A/B acceptance & rollback plan
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara@acmecorp.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Promptset regression observed after model update — request for A/B plan

Hi Dylan,

We rolled the model update last week and are seeing a subtle, but customer-visible, regression on our product search assistant for a small subset of prompts (attached sample). Accuracy on product attribute extraction dropped ~6% for the test prompts in tier-B customers.

Can your team help wire an A/B that pins the prior model for a control group while we run a short eval on the new promptset? We need clear acceptance criteria (metrics and thresholds), a rollout plan (percentages + timing), and an explicit rollback trigger. Our CS manager wants something we can show during the 6/7 sync.

Attached: promptset_v3.csv (sample prompts flagged).

Thanks — appreciate the quick help.

— Sara Liu
Product Ops, Acme Retail

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme regression — draft acceptance criteria & AB rollout (need owners)

Team — follow-up from Sara at Acme. They reported a ~6% drop for a subset of prompts after our model bump. We need a crisp, operational plan we can give Acme by EOD tomorrow and present in their 6/7 sync.

What I’m asking for:
- Marissa: draft acceptance metrics and thresholds (precision/recall/QA score) and the comparison window.
- Jonas: outline rollout gating and what runtime telemetry we must collect (latency, top-k mismatch, token-level quality signals).
- Laura: legal/compliance check for pinning older model for a control cohort and any procurement/contract notes.
- Dev: estimate the implementation lift to run AB with automatic rollback hooks in Redwood Console (and whether we can use existing canary routes).

Proposal (first-pass):
- Evaluation metric: weighted QA F1 on labeled subset + human evaluation pass on 200 items.
- Acceptance threshold: new_model >= baseline_model - 2% absolute on weighted F1 AND no regression >5% on any critical intent bucket.
- Rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 24-48h windows if gates pass. Immediate rollback to baseline for any 1h window where failure condition triggers.

Attachments: ab_plan_v1.docx, eval_metrics_template.xlsx.

Callout: We should include an escape hatch (manual override + instant routing to a fallback variant) and tie the rollback to both automated metric thresholds and an on-call approval.

Can each of you reply with acceptance/oppose + suggested edits by 3pm PT today? I’ll consolidate and send to Acme.

Thanks — Dylan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T13:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme regression — draft acceptance criteria & AB rollout (need owners)

Thanks Dylan. Quick edits and clarifications from Evals: 

Suggested metrics (ranked):
- Primary: weighted F1 on labeled prompts (weighting by customer impact buckets).
- Secondary: prompt-level BLEU/ROUGE is noisy; prefer per-intent confusion rate and token-level hallucination flags.
- Human eval: 3-judge majority on a 5-point relevance scale, sample size = 200 (stratified).

Acceptance thresholds (conservative):
- New_model >= baseline - 1.5% absolute on weighted F1 over the 48h test window.
- No intent bucket shows >4% absolute regression.
- No increase in hallucination signal rate by >25% relative.

Rollout plan: keep your percentages but extend observation windows: 5% (12h) -> 25% (24h) -> 50% (24h). Gate evaluation at the end of each window with automated checks plus a single human QA sign-off before moving to 50%.

Rollback: automated rollback on metric breach; manual override stays with customer success + on-call lead. We should also enable a short warm-start pin for control cohort (to make comparisons stable).

I’ll populate the eval_metrics_template.xlsx with the exact query set and scoring scripts by EOD.

— Marissa
Evals Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-31T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme regression — draft acceptance criteria & AB rollout (need owners)

Quick notes on implementation and observability:

- Telemetry: we must capture per-request model_id, prompt_hash, latency_ms, top_3_candidates (hash), and the eval_score metadata from the scoring pipeline. These enable quick triage for skew.
- Alerts: wire a short-term alert for 1h windows where weighted F1 delta <= -2% or per-intent delta <= -3%. Keep alert sensitivity adjustable for the first 24h.
- Rollback automation: Redwood Console supports an automated rollback policy tied to metric streams. Dev — do we have the infra hooks to run the automatic revert + traffic re-route within the proposed windows? If not, we should plan a manual fallback for the first rollout step.

Also: run a small shadow run (no routing change) for 6h to collect baseline signals if Acme can tolerate the delay — this reduces false positives.

On the quoting style:
> On Mon, May 30, 2027 at 11:30 AM Dylan Brooks wrote:
> 
> Proposal (first-pass):
> - Evaluation metric: weighted QA F1 on labeled subset + human evaluation pass on 200 items.

Agree with primary metric; adding the shadow run will make the acceptance clearer.

— Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Promptset regression observed after model update — A/B plan and next steps

Sara — thanks for the patience. Summary of agreed plan and owners below so you can share with your CS manager at the 6/7 sync.

What we’ll run (agreed):
- Metric & sample: weighted F1 on labeled subset (200 stratified items) + 3-judge human eval on the same sample. Marissa owns scoring and the sample.
- Shadow run: 6h shadow collection to stabilize signals before traffic splits (Jonas + Dev to run).
- Rollout: 5% (12h) -> 25% (24h) -> 50% (24h) with gate checks at the end of each window.
- Acceptance gates: new_model >= baseline - 1.5% weighted F1; no intent bucket >4% regression; no hallucination signal >25% increase.
- Rollback: automated rollback on metric breach OR manual rollback triggered by CS + on-call. Dev will enable an immediate routing fallback.

Owners / deliverables:
- Marissa Cole: populate eval_metrics_template.xlsx and run the labeling/human evaluation (deliver by 6/3 EOD).
- Jonas Weber: telemetry + alerting setup (deliver by 6/3 morning).
- Dev Patel: implement the AB route + rollback hooks in Redwood Console; confirm whether initial step will be manual or automated (deliver by 6/3 EOD).
- Dylan Brooks: consolidate and send to Acme; coordinate the 6/7 sync.

Links & references: HubSpot record https://hubspot.com/contacts/ACME-3456; Jira ticket https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/EVAL-879. Attachments: ab_plan_v1.docx, eval_metrics_template.xlsx.

Sara — are you good with this timeline? If yes, I’ll schedule the shadow run for 6/3 10:00 PT and share the console route for verification.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
